claim: criminal charges for trafficking in a dangerous drug

facts.F1: On 19 April 2017, a number of officers were engaged in an anti-narcotics operation in the vicinity of Hing Wah Car Park at Wan Tsui Road, Chai Wan.
facts.F2: At around 10:18 pm, Wong Man Piu was seen by officer DPC8964 to have mounted the driver’s seat of a private motor vehicle with the registration number UP5672.
facts.F3: The defendant was intercepted by another officer of the team, DPC8259, about five minutes later and, on a body search, he was found to have in his possession a phone, a little over $500 in cash, and a key for the car.
facts.F4: Armed with a search warrant, the officers then went on to search the car and they found in the course of that search a bag hidden underneath the steering wheel near the foot pedals of the vehicle.
facts.F5: This bag was later sent to the government chemist for examination and it was confirmed that the bag has inside 43 smaller plastic bags containing a total of 8.39 grammes of a solid containing 7.81 grammes of cocaine.
facts.F6: At around 10:45 the same evening, Wong Man Piu was arrested by DPC8964 for the offence of trafficking in a dangerous drug.
facts.F7: Under caution, the defendant stated that the cocaine belonged to him and was for his own consumption.
facts.F8: The defendant repeated that the cocaine was for his own consumption, that this was bought by him from a friend called “Ah Lung” on 31 March 2017 at $5,300, in a video interview which took place in the evening of 20 April 2017.
facts.F9: The defendant hid the dangerous drugs under the driving wheel of the vehicle.
facts.F10: The defendant told the police that the drugs would have lasted him for about a month and he also told the police in the same interview that he was working as a transportation worker, earning about 9 to 10 thousand dollars per month.
facts.F11: The police estimated the street value for the cocaine found on the car was about $7,700.
facts.F12: The defendant pleaded guilty to the charge of trafficking and, as confirmed by Mr Lau, solicitor appearing for him, it is now accepted by the defendant that the drugs were actually for the purpose of trafficking, although a portion of it was to be retained for his own consumption.
facts.F13: The defendant is now 30 years old, locally born and bred, left school after finishing Form 2 and had since been working as a transportation worker, and is married for 9 to 10 years and is living with his wife, two young daughters aged 4 and 8 respectively, and his parents at a unit in a government housing estate in Chai Wan.
facts.F14: The defendant has one previous conviction for claiming to be a member of a triad society, entered in 2008 when he was only about 19 years old.
facts.F15: The defendant’s father handed up a letter, telling the court also about his own failing health.
facts.F16: Letters from the defendant’s wife and his employer spoke positively about the defendant but made no mention of his addiction the defendant had to drugs which, according to what was told, the defendant had been suffering from for about 10 years.
facts.F17: The court considered the starting point for sentencing for trafficking in heroin and/or cocaine of up to 10 grammes.
facts.F18: The standard sentence for this is as per the tariffs established in Lau Tak Ming.
facts.F19: The defendant was given a starting sentence of 51 months before discounts.
facts.F20: The sentence was reduced due to the guilty plea, possible self-consumption, and delay in bringing the case to court.

Whether the defendant had an addiction problem
